annotation.title_clean: Conseil d'État, juge des référés, ordonnance du 18 mai 2020, n° 440442 et 440445, Association La Quadrature du Net et autre (surveillance par drones)
annotation.title_en: Council of State, Summary Judge Order of 18 May 2020, No. 440442 and 440445, La Quadrature du Net and another (drone surveillance)
annotation.summary_en: French Conseil d'État interim-relief order finding that Paris police drone surveillance of COVID-19 lockdown compliance processed personal data without a prior regulatory authorisation after CNIL opinion, a grave and manifestly illegal infringement of privacy. It orders the State to stop the drone surveillance until a legal text is adopted or drones are technically unable to identify people.
key_provisions_or_claims: Drone images, given zoom and lack of anti-identification safeguards, are personal data processing under Directive 2016/680.
Processing without a regulatory text authorising it (after CNIL opinion, Art. 31 Loi Informatique et Libertés) infringes privacy grave and manifestly illegally.
State ordered to cease drone surveillance in Paris until a regulatory text is issued or technical means make identification impossible.
The purpose (detecting gatherings for public health) is legitimate, but a legal framework is required.
Privacy and freedom of movement are fundamental freedoms under Art. L. 521-2 CJA.
